input.question: How do Yelp, Google, etc. verify a business is closed when it is reported as closed by users?
input.ground_truth: When my restaurant opened we had a hell of a time getting Google to update with correct hours. We were submitting complaints/queries everyday. We know there were times it hurt us. So my guess is no, they do not verify, but I don't know for sure.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: How do Yelp, Google, etc. verify a business is closed when it is reported as closed by users?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a lemonade stand. If someone tells a big book (like Yelp or Google) that your lemonade stand is closed, the big book doesn’t just believe them right away. Instead, it checks with other people and maybe even looks at your stand to see if the sign is down or the door is locked.

Sometimes, the big book also asks you, the person who runs the stand, “Is your stand closed?” You can tell them “Yes, I’m closed for a nap!” or “No, I’m open for lemonade!”

So, they check with people and maybe look at your stand to make sure it’s really closed before they tell everyone it’s closed. That way, nobody gets confused about whether you’re selling lemonade or taking a break!
